{{Nihongo|'''Akira Tonomura'''|外村 彰|Tonomura Akira|April 25, 1942&nbsp;– May 2, 2012}} was a Japanese [[physicist]], best known for his development of [[electron holography]] and his experimental verification of the [[Aharonov–Bohm effect]].<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Howie | first1 = A.| title = Akira Tonomura (1942–2012) | doi = 10.1038/486324a | journal = Nature | volume = 486 | issue = 7403 | pages = 324 | year = 2012 | pmid =  22722184| bibcode = 2012Natur.486..324H| doi-access = free }}</ref>

==Biography==
Tonomura was born in [[Hyōgo]], Japan, and graduated from [[the University of Tokyo]] with a degree in physics. Upon graduation he joined the [[Hitachi]] Central Research Laboratory, where he later attained the title "Fellow" in 1999.<ref>[http://www.hitachi.com/rd/fellow_tonomura.html Hitachi Fellow: Dr. TONOMURA Akira] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515210718/http://www.hitachi.com/rd/fellow_tonomura.html |date=May 15, 2012 }}</ref>

In the 1970s, Tonomura did pioneering work in the development of the [[electron holography]] microscope and observed lines of magnetic force for the first time in the world. Building on this, in 1986, he experimentally verified the [[Aharonov–Bohm effect]], which had eluded definitive experimental proof for a long time. This experiment proved that [[vector potential]]s, which are nothing more than a mathematical concept in [[classical physics]], are in fact physical quantities that are more fundamental (i.e. have [[ontological priority]]) than electric or magnetic fields.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hitachi.com/rd/fellow_tono_bio.html |title=Biography: Dr. TONOMURA Akira |access-date=May 5, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081224011822/http://www.hitachi.com/rd/fellow_tono_bio.html |archive-date=December 24, 2008 |publisher=Hitachi}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1073/pnas.0506215102|pmid=16217037|pmc=1257714|title=Profile of Akira Tonomura|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=102|issue=42|pages=14949–14951|year=2005|last1=Downey|first1=P.|bibcode=2005PNAS..10214949D|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Tonomura | first1=Akira | last2=Osakabe | first2=Nobuyuki | last3=Matsuda | first3=Tsuyoshi | last4=Kawasaki | first4=Takeshi | last5=Endo | first5=Junji | last6=Yano | first6=Shinichiro | last7=Yamada | first7=Hiroji | title=Evidence for Aharonov-Bohm effect with magnetic field completely shielded from electron wave | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=56 | issue=8 | date=1986-02-24 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.56.792 | pages=792–795| pmid=10033287 | bibcode=1986PhRvL..56..792T }}</ref>

Tonomura was also known for his observations of magnetic vortex movement in [[superconductor]]s.
